date: "2023-04-12"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
if (!require("data.table")) {
  install.packages("data.table")
  library(data.table)
}

# Set the folder path
folder_path <- "Assets and Liabilities"

# List all CSV files in the folder
all_files <- list.files(path = folder_path, pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE)

# Read all files into a list of data.tables
data_tables_list <- lapply(all_files, function(x) fread(x, fill = TRUE, verbose = FALSE))

# Identify unique columns across all CSV files, excluding "cert"
all_columns <- unique(unlist(lapply(data_tables_list, function(dt) setdiff(colnames(dt), "cert"))))

# Initialize an empty list to store the merged datasets
merged_data_list <- list()

# Iterate through each data.table in the list
for (dt in data_tables_list) {
  # Set the key for the data.table to "cert"
  setkey(dt, cert)
  
  # Check if the merged_data_list is empty
  if (length(merged_data_list) == 0) {
    # Assign the current data.table to the merged_data_list
    merged_data_list <- dt
  } else {
    # Perform a left join with the current data.table based on the "cert" key
    merged_data_list <- merged_data_list[dt, on = "cert"]
  }
  
  # Retain only the columns from the current data.table and the "cert" column
  setcolorder(merged_data_list, c("cert", setdiff(colnames(dt), "cert")))
}

# Convert the merged data.table to a data.frame
merged_data <- as.data.frame(merged_data_list)

# Save the merged data as a new CSV file if desired
write.csv(merged_data, "Merged_Assets_Liabilities.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
